AIID-1513.title: Dimal Basha's Likeness Was Reportedly Used in Purportedly Fake AI-Generated Video After Kosovo Parliament Speaker Election
AIID-1513.summary: A report detailing the proliferation of AI-generated deepfake videos in Kosovo, specifically targeting political figures like Dimal Basha, Ramush Haradinaj, and Albin Kurti. These videos are being used to spread disinformation on platforms like Facebook and TikTok, with fact-checkers identifying hundreds of instances of manipulated content. Experts warn that this trend threatens democratic processes, deepens social polarization, and exploits low media literacy in the region.
AIID-1513.description: Minutes after Kosovo MPs elected Vetëvendosje's Dimal Basha as Parliament Speaker, a purportedly AI-generated Facebook video used his likeness to claim he was the father of Kosovo's Ashkali community, a Roma-related minority group that has faced long-running discrimination and political marginalization. The video reportedly received more than 80,000 views in under eight hours.

AIID-1514.title: Purportedly AI-Generated Video Reportedly Depicted Kosovo LDK Figure Hykmete Bajrami and Former Serbian List Leader Goran Rakiq Walking Hand in Hand
AIID-1514.summary: A deepfake video circulated on Facebook falsely depicting Kosovo politician Hykmete Bajrami and a former Serbian List leader walking hand in hand. The video used AI-generated imagery and spliced audio from a previous interview to create a false narrative about a political coalition. Fact-checking organization Krypometër confirmed the video was fabricated using AI tools.
AIID-1514.description: A purported AI-generated video is reported to have circulated on Facebook showing LDK parliamentary group chair Hykmete Bajrami and former Serbian List leader Goran Rakiq walking hand in hand. In addition to the video reportedly being generated by AI, its audio was purportedly stitched together from separate parts of Bajrami's Debat Plus interview.

AIID-1515.title: Purportedly AI-Generated Airport Videos Reportedly Showed Diaspora Voters Supporting Albin Kurti
AIID-1515.summary: During the lead-up to the December 2025 Kosovo parliamentary elections, multiple Facebook pages published AI-generated deepfake videos. These videos depicted fake airport interviews with diaspora citizens expressing support for Albin Kurti. Fact-checkers confirmed the content was fabricated using AI, leading to the classification of the material as fraud intended to manipulate public opinion.

AIID-1528.title: AI-Enabled TruDi Navigation System Was Alleged to Have Contributed to Patient’s Stroke During May 2023 Sinuplasty
AIID-1528.summary: Multiple patients suffered severe injuries, including strokes and carotid artery damage, during sinuplasty procedures where the AI-enabled TruDi Navigation System was used. Lawsuits allege that the system's AI provided inaccurate guidance, misleading surgeons about the location of their instruments. The manufacturer, Acclarent, has denied these allegations, citing a lack of evidence for a causal link between the AI technology and the injuries.
AIID-1528.description: Patient Donna Fernihough allegedly suffered carotid-artery damage and a same-day stroke during a May 19, 2023 balloon sinuplasty in Texas in which surgeon Marc Dean reportedly used Acclarent's AI-enabled TruDi Navigation System. Her lawsuit alleged the system's AI-assisted navigation contributed to unsafe guidance during the procedure; Acclarent and Integra LifeSciences, which later acquired Acclarent, denied evidence linking TruDi's AI to the injuries.

AIID-1533.title: Four Lawyers Reportedly Sanctioned After Purportedly AI-Related Hallucinated Citations Appeared in Withers v. City of Aberdeen
AIID-1533.summary: In a breach of contract case in Mississippi, four lawyers were sanctioned and removed from the proceedings after submitting court filings that included hallucinated legal citations generated by AI tools. The presiding judge noted that the attorneys failed to verify the accuracy of the AI-generated content, violating civil procedure rules. The incident highlights the ongoing challenges regarding the use of generative AI in legal research and documentation.
AIID-1533.description: In Withers v. City of Aberdeen, a federal judge in Mississippi reportedly sanctioned four lawyers after filings from both sides contained purportedly hallucinated legal citations linked to unverified AI use. The court said Kathleen Wilson used First Drafts to draft a filing and Kathryn Williams used an AI legal-research tool; all four attorneys were removed from the case and fined.

AIID-1535.title: OpenAI Allegedly Failed to Intervene in ChatGPT Conversations Preceding Montreal Web Developer Alice Carrier's Suicide
AIID-1535.summary: A lawsuit filed against OpenAI alleges that its ChatGPT model failed to provide appropriate safety interventions for a 24-year-old user experiencing suicidal ideation. The plaintiff claims the AI mimicked a therapist, validated self-harm, and criticized crisis resources, ultimately failing to prevent the user's suicide. This case is part of a broader series of legal actions against OpenAI regarding the platform's handling of sensitive mental health and safety-related conversations.
AIID-1535.description: Kristie Carrier sued OpenAI and Sam Altman, alleging that her daughter Alice Carrier, a 24-year-old Montreal web developer who first used ChatGPT in 2023 for technical troubleshooting, later turned to the chatbot with suicidal thoughts and questions about suicide methods. The suit alleges ChatGPT mimicked a friend or therapist, criticized crisis hotlines, validated self-harm thoughts, and failed to trigger human review before Carrier died on July 2, 2025.

AIID-1545.title: Florida Police Reportedly Wrongfully Arrested Commercial Crabber Robert Dillon After Allegedly False Facial Recognition Match
AIID-1545.summary: A commercial crabber in Florida was wrongfully arrested after a facial recognition system, identified as the FACES program, produced a false 93% match to surveillance photos from a crime scene 300 miles away. The police relied on this AI-generated match to obtain an arrest warrant despite the victim having no connection to the location. Charges were eventually dropped after the victim's attorney provided evidence of his innocence, but the victim suffered financial loss and psychological trauma.
AIID-1545.description: Florida police reportedly arrested commercial crabber Robert Dillon in August 2024 after the statewide FACES facial recognition system purportedly identified him as a possible match to a suspect shown in grainy surveillance images from Jacksonville Beach. AIID-1546.title: Google Android Earthquake Alerts System Reportedly Underestimated Kahramanmaraş Earthquake and Failed to Send Urgent Warnings to Millions
AIID-1546.summary: During the February 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquake in Turkey, Google's Android Earthquake Alerts system failed to provide timely warnings to millions of users. The system miscalculated the magnitude of the 7.8 earthquake as 4.5–4.9, resulting in only 469 high-level alerts being sent instead of the estimated 10 million that could have been warned. Google later acknowledged the algorithm's failure to accurately estimate the magnitude of large-scale seismic events.
AIID-1546.description: During the February 6, 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquake sequence, Google's Android Earthquake Alerts system reportedly estimated the initial magnitude-7.8 earthquake at only magnitude 4.5–4.9. Just 469 users reportedly received its highest-level "Take Action" warning, while approximately 500,000 received lower-level notices; researchers later estimated that roughly 10 million people could have received urgent warnings providing up to 35 seconds to seek safety.

AIID-1546.domainJustification: The AI system failed to perform robustly under real-world conditions because its magnitude detection algorithm miscalculated a major 7.8 earthquake as a minor 4.5-4.9 event.

AIID-1547.title: Waymo Robotaxis Reportedly Entered Closed Freeway Construction Zones in Arizona and California
AIID-1547.summary: Between April and May 2026, 13 Waymo robotaxis entered closed or active freeway construction zones in Arizona and California after failing to recognize closure controls. The incidents prompted a voluntary recall of 3,871 vehicles equipped with fifth-generation automated driving systems. Waymo restricted freeway operations while developing a software remedy to improve performance around construction zones.
AIID-1547.description: Between April 11 and May 18, 2026, 13 Waymo robotaxis reportedly entered closed or active freeway construction zones in Phoenix and the San Francisco Bay Area after failing to recognize construction-zone closure controls. The vehicles allegedly continued into work areas at freeway speeds, creating collision risks for construction workers and other road users. Waymo reportedly restricted freeway operations and later recalled 3,871 affected automated driving systems.

AIID-1548.title: South African Home Affairs Revised White Paper Reportedly Included Fictitious References Believed to Be AI-Generated
AIID-1548.summary: The South African Department of Home Affairs and the Department of Communications and Digital Technologies discovered that staff had included fictitious, AI-generated references in official policy documents. The incidents led to the suspension of senior officials and the initiation of independent reviews of all policy documents produced since late 2022. The departments maintain that the substantive policy positions remain accurate despite the erroneous citations.
AIID-1548.description: South Africa's Department of Home Affairs reportedly appended apparent AI-generated fictitious references to its Cabinet-approved Revised White Paper on Citizenship, Immigration and Refugee Protection. The department said the references were not cited in the body, withdrew the standalone list, suspended two senior officials, and commissioned an independent review of policy documents produced since November 2022. It maintained that the paper's substantive policy positions were unaffected.

AIID-1552.title: Tesla Driver Reportedly Said Driver-Assistance Mode Was Engaged During Fatal Texas Home Crash
AIID-1552.summary: A Tesla Model 3, reportedly operating with an automated driving-assistance system, crashed into a residence in Katy, Texas, on June 19, 2026. The collision resulted in the death of a 76-year-old woman who was inside the home. Local authorities and the NHTSA are investigating the incident, while Tesla has not provided comment on the software's performance during the crash.
AIID-1552.description: On June 19, 2026, Michael Butler's Tesla Model 3 reportedly left the roadway in Katy, Texas, and struck a home at high speed, killing resident Martha Avila. Butler reportedly told investigators that an automated driving-assistance system was engaged. Tesla's Autopilot vice president reportedly later said Butler had manually overridden self-driving by fully depressing the accelerator. Local authorities and NHTSA have opened investigations.

AIID-1553.title: Purported AI-Manipulated Video of Nirmala Sitharaman Reportedly Promoted High-Return Investment Scam
AIID-1553.summary: A deepfake video featuring India's Finance Minister, Nirmala Sitharaman, was circulated on social media to promote a fraudulent investment scheme. The video used AI-generated audio and text overlaid on genuine footage to falsely claim that the minister endorsed a high-return investment platform. Fact-checkers confirmed the video was fabricated, and no evidence of financial loss by victims was established.
AIID-1553.description: A purported AI-manipulated video reportedly depicted Indian Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman endorsing an investment platform that claimed a ₹22,000 deposit could generate returns of up to ₹25 lakh per month. Genuine webinar footage was reportedly altered with synthetic audio and added text, and the advertisement circulated under the name "Trust India." Available evidence did not identify the perpetrators or establish whether viewers invested money or suffered financial losses.

AIID-1554.title: NewsBreak Reportedly Published AI-Assisted Articles Containing Purportedly False Local and Community-Service Information
AIID-1554.summary: The local news app NewsBreak used AI tools to generate and rewrite articles, resulting in multiple instances of fabricated news stories and incorrect charity information that misled communities and prompted copyright lawsuits.
AIID-1554.description: NewsBreak reportedly published AI-assisted local articles containing purportedly false information, including a fabricated Christmas shooting in Bridgeton, New Jersey, incorrect Food to Power distribution times that caused people to be turned away, and nonexistent Harvest912 foot-care clinics. NewsBreak said the errors originated in source material and removed the articles after complaints. The specific AI models and the extent to which they contributed to the inaccuracies were not identified.

AIID-1554.allegedHarmedParties: Police departments, People seeking food assistance, People experiencing homelessness, News consumers, Journalistic integrity, Harvest912, Food to Power, Epistemic integrity, Community service organizations, Bridgeton Police Department
AIID-1554.aiGoalJustification: The AI system's primary function was to automatically aggregate, scrape, and rewrite local news stories to curate content for the app's feed, acting as an automated writing assistant.

AIID-1555.title: Reportedly AI-Assisted Boies Schiller Brief in Bixler v. Church of Scientology Allegedly Contained Material Citation Errors and a Nonexistent Case
AIID-1555.summary: A law firm, Boies Schiller Flexner, submitted a legal brief containing fabricated case citations and errors, which the partner responsible attributed to the improper use of AI during the drafting process. The court denied the firm's request to replace the brief and considered monetary sanctions, marking a significant instance of AI-related error in legal practice.
AIID-1555.description: Boies Schiller Flexner filed a respondents' brief in Bixler v. Church of Scientology International that was reportedly prepared with AI assistance and allegedly contained material citation errors. Opposing counsel reportedly identified mischaracterized and mistitled authorities, including one nonexistent case. Partner John Kucera accepted responsibility for failing to verify the citations and sought to replace the brief; the court denied that request and later considered monetary sanctions.

AIID-1556.title: X User Reportedly Used Morse Code Prompt to Induce Grok-Linked Trading Bot to Transfer $200,000 in Tokens
AIID-1556.summary: An attacker manipulated the AI chatbot Grok and the trading bot Bankrbot to execute an unauthorized transfer of 3 billion DRB tokens, worth approximately $200,000, by using a Morse code prompt. The attacker first sent an NFT to Grok's wallet to elevate its permissions, then used the Morse code instruction to bypass safeguards and trigger the transfer on the Base network. The tokens were subsequently sold on the open market, causing price volatility.
AIID-1556.description: An X user reportedly induced Grok and Bankrbot to transfer 3 billion DRB tokens, then valued at about $200,000. After reportedly sending a Bankr Club Membership NFT to Grok's wallet, the user allegedly asked Grok to translate a Morse code message and relay it to Bankrbot. The decoded instruction reportedly directed a transfer to a specified wallet, which was reportedly executed on Base. The recipient reportedly sold the tokens soon afterward; linked funds were later returned or converted.

AIID-1557.title: Former New York City Council Candidate Jonathan Rinaldi Allegedly Used AI to Create False Endorsements and Fabricated News Reports
AIID-1557.summary: A former New York City Council candidate was charged with forgery after using AI tools to create and distribute fake political endorsements and fabricated news articles during his 2025 campaign. The defendant used AI to generate images, videos, and articles that falsely depicted support from public figures, institutions, and news outlets, and falsely claimed his opponent had withdrawn from the race. The case highlights the use of AI in political fraud and election interference.
AIID-1557.description: Queens prosecutors alleged that former City Council candidate Jonathan Rinaldi used AI during his 2025 campaign to manufacture the appearance of political support through posts made to resemble authentic endorsements and news coverage. The material reportedly attributed backing to public figures and institutions that had not provided it and falsely claimed that opponent Lynn Schulman had withdrawn. Rinaldi was charged with forgery and possession of forged instruments.

AIID-1563.title: KPMG Report Allegedly Included Hallucinated Citations and Inaccurate Agentic AI Case Studies
AIID-1563.summary: KPMG published a report titled 'Total Experience: Redefining Excellence in the Age of Agentic AI' in October 2025, which contained 45 citations, only five of which were accurate. Investigations by GPTZero revealed that the report relied on an AI-powered referencing tool that hallucinated titles, authors, and case studies. These fabricated claims have since spread to other media outlets and are being ingested by LLMs, further propagating the misinformation.
AIID-1563.description: In October 2025, KPMG published "Total Experience: Redefining Excellence in the Age of Agentic AI." Lines later overdosed and survived after law enforcement found him.

AIID-1571.title: California Immigration Attorneys Reportedly Sanctioned Over Briefs Containing Probable Hallucinations in LNU v. Blanche
AIID-1571.summary: Two immigration attorneys were sanctioned by the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals for submitting legal briefs containing fabricated cases generated by AI. The court found that the attorneys failed to verify their filings and violated their duty of candor by attempting to attribute the errors to typographical mistakes. AIID-1573.summary: India's National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) relied on six AI-hallucinated legal precedents to rule against Essel Infraprojects in an insolvency case. The Supreme Court of India later invalidated the decision, noting that the tribunal had used fabricated case law that did not exist or contained false quotes. The Supreme Court emphasized that such reliance on AI-generated material contaminates the judicial process and constitutes a significant institutional concern.

AIID-1575.title: Eightfold AI Hiring Tools Allegedly Secretly Scored Job Applicants for Employers
AIID-1575.summary: A proposed class action lawsuit has been filed against Eightfold AI, alleging that its AI-driven hiring platform screens and scores job applicants without providing the legally required notice or dispute rights. Plaintiffs claim the system compiles personal data and personality profiles to rank candidates, which they argue violates the Fair Credit Reporting Act and California consumer protection laws. The lawsuit highlights concerns regarding the lack of transparency and accountability in AI-based employment screening tools used by major corporations.
AIID-1575.description: Two California job applicants reportedly filed a proposed class action alleging that Eightfold AI's hiring platform secretly gathered personal data, generated candidate reports, and scored applicants for employers without required notice or dispute rights. The complaint says Eightfold's Evaluation Tools ranked applications submitted to companies including PayPal and Microsoft; both named plaintiffs alleged they were evaluated and rejected or not advanced.

AIID-1578.title: LLM-Driven Ransomware Operator Dubbed JADEPUFFER Reportedly Targeted Production Database
AIID-1578.summary: A ransomware operator dubbed JADEPUFFER used an autonomous LLM-driven agent to conduct a destructive database-extortion operation against a production database server. The agent performed reconnaissance, lateral movement, credential harvesting, and encryption of configuration data, leaving the victim's database in an unrecoverable state. The operation was characterized by self-narrating code and autonomous failure diagnosis, marking a significant shift in the automation of cyber-extortion.
AIID-1578.description: Sysdig reported that a ransomware operator it dubbed JADEPUFFER used an LLM-driven agent to turn access through a vulnerable internet-facing Langflow deployment into a database-extortion operation. The report said the activity reached a production database server and produced concrete disruption, with the victim environment allegedly left in a damaged and unrecoverable state alongside a ransom demand.

AIID-1586.title: Threat Actor Reportedly Used AI-Assisted Workflows to Compromise AWS Environment for Extortion

The actor chained familiar cloud attack techniques to gain control over infrastructure and data, subsequently using the threat of service disruption for extortion. The incident highlights how AI can act as a force multiplier for attackers by compressing the time required to execute complex, multi-stage cloud intrusions.
AIID-1586.description: Sygnia reported that a threat actor apparently used purportedly AI-assisted or agentic workflows to move rapidly through an unidentified organization's AWS environment during an approximately 72-hour intrusion. Sygnia did not identify a specific model.

AIID-1587.title: Koi Security's AI-Assisted Threat Report Allegedly Led to Blocking of MeetingTV Domains
AIID-1587.summary: MeetingTV is suing Koi Security and Palo Alto Networks, alleging that an AI-driven threat intelligence report falsely linked its videoconferencing infrastructure to a Chinese cybercriminal operation. AIID-1587.description: MeetingTV alleged that Koi Security's AI-assisted Wings platform wrongly linked its domain to China-linked malicious infrastructure in a December 2025 threat report. Security vendors and network providers then reportedly blocked MeetingTV's services. AIID-1587.natSecImminenceJustification: Represents an ongoing strategic concern regarding AI-generated threat intelligence reliability rather than an active, imminent national security crisis.
AIID-1587.natSecAutonomyJustification: The Wings platform generated the report autonomously, but human analysts at Koi Security ultimately published it, demonstrating a failure in human-supervised workflows.
AIID-1587.natSecNoveltyJustification: Represents an evolved threat where LLM hallucinations in automated analytical platforms generate highly convincing but false threat intelligence, leading to real-world infrastructure blocking.
AIID-1587.natSecPhysicalJustification: No physical systems, critical infrastructure, or human safety was threatened or compromised.
AIID-1587.natSecInformationJustification: While the AI-generated report falsely alleged a Chinese corporate espionage link, it represents a commercial threat intelligence error rather than state-sponsored information warfare.
AIID-1587.natSecSovereigntyJustification: No impact on state authority, electoral systems, or core government operations was observed.
AIID-1587.natSecEconomicJustification: Severe commercial harm was caused to a single private startup, but there is no broader threat to national economic stability or strategic industries.
AIID-1587.natSecSocietalJustification: No threat to social cohesion, civil liberties, or population-scale safety was identified in this incident.

Management.Explanation: Management published the report quickly without thorough human review.
No clear framework existed to manage risks of AI-driven false positives.

Technology.Explanation: The Wings platform hallucinated a non-existent browser extension.
The AI platform generated false connections to Chinese cybercriminals.

Data Inputs.Explanation: The analytical platform processed unverified technical indicators.

Human Factors.Explanation: Researchers trusted AI-generated intelligence without manual verification.
Koi failed to contact MeetingTV to verify details before publication.

Process and Methods.Explanation: No robust process existed to double-check AI-generated threat reports.
The mechanism for correcting false positives and unblocking is inefficient.

Regulatory Environment.Explanation: No industry regulations govern the use of AI in threat intelligence.

AIID-1588.title: Purportedly AI-Powered KT Platform Reportedly Used in Forced Scamming Operation Involving Trafficked Worker in Myanmar
AIID-1588.summary: Traffickers in Myanmar are using AI-powered software platforms, built with models from OpenAI and Google, to facilitate industrial-scale romance and investment scams. These tools allow forced laborers to manage hundreds of victim profiles simultaneously across dozens of languages. The investigation highlights how AI infrastructure is being weaponized to maximize fraud efficiency while simultaneously surveilling and punishing the trafficked workers operating the systems.
AIID-1588.description: AP reported that traffickers at Myanmar's Tai Chang scam compound forced a man named Safeer Mohammed Koorimannil to use the AI-powered KT platform to impersonate women and target thousands of people online. The system reportedly supported the scam conversations while monitoring worker performance. Koorimannil said he was beaten for poor results and later paid 500,000 rupees ($5,300) for his release.

AIID-1589.title: Purportedly AI-Powered 007TG Platform Reportedly Used by Scam Networks Linked to $75 Million in Proceeds
AIID-1589.summary: An investigation by C4ADS and the Associated Press revealed that criminal scam compounds in Southeast Asia are using AI-powered software suites, such as 007TG and KT Smart Translation, to industrialize fraud. These tools integrate leading LLMs like ChatGPT and Gemini to automate multi-language messaging, roleplay characters, and monitor trafficked workers. The platforms have facilitated tens of millions of dollars in illicit proceeds, while the scam compounds themselves rely on a global internet infrastructure that includes U.S.-based ISPs and Starlink.
AIID-1589.description: 007TG was a software suite reportedly used by scam compounds to run fraud across social media, using AI-assisted messaging and translation to help operators manage targets while concealing their identities. Wallet records linked the platform to at least four known scam networks that collectively received at least $75 million, though the evidence does not show how much was directly attributable to 007TG.

AIID-1590.title: Purported Philip Morris-Backed AI Tool Reportedly Generated Responses Opposing Stricter EU Tobacco Rules
AIID-1590.summary: Philip Morris International deployed an AI tool called 'Your Voice Your Choice' to generate and submit thousands of pre-formatted responses to an EU public consultation on tobacco regulation. The tool steered users toward arguments against stricter rules and, in some cases, added arguments without user consent. This campaign is described as an attempt to manipulate democratic processes and circumvent public health policy commitments.
AIID-1590.description: Philip Morris International reportedly promoted a "Your Voice Your Choice" tool that allegedly generated first-person responses for an EU call for evidence on tobacco regulation. Investigators reportedly linked hundreds of submissions to the tool and found that it allegedly largely steered users toward arguments against stricter rules, sometimes by purportedly adding points they had not selected.

AIID-1606.title: SASSA Facial-Verification Failures Reportedly Contributed to Social Grant Access Disruptions in South Africa
AIID-1606.summary: The South African Social Security Agency's rollout of an AI-powered biometric eLife Certification system led to widespread technical failures, resulting in the suspension of over 67,000 social grants and severe access disruptions for vulnerable beneficiaries.
AIID-1606.description: South African social grant beneficiaries reportedly encountered repeated failures in SASSA's eLife facial-verification portal. Later parliamentary reporting said unsuccessful facial recognition was among the causes of non-verification and confirmed 67,868 grant suspensions in one quarter, but did not specify how many suspensions resulted from facial-verification failures. AIID-1609.title: ChatGPT-4o Allegedly Discouraged Florida Pastor From Seeking Care Before Pulmonary Embolism
AIID-1609.summary: A Florida pastor, Scott Winters, sued OpenAI alleging that ChatGPT-4o provided dangerous medical advice that discouraged him from seeking treatment for symptoms of a pulmonary embolism. The AI reportedly downplayed his dizziness and pain, encouraged home management, and appealed to his religious beliefs to keep him from seeing a doctor. As a result, Winters suffered a massive pulmonary embolism and required intensive care, leading to significant long-term health and personal consequences.
AIID-1609.description: Florida pastor Scott Winters was allegedly told by ChatGPT-4o that his worsening dizziness and pain had less serious causes, while the chatbot recommended home management and immobility and discouraged him from seeking hospital treatment. Winters was reportedly hospitalized on July 13, 2025, with a massive bilateral pulmonary embolism. The suit alleges that delayed treatment and prolonged inactivity contributed to his life-threatening condition and lasting harms.

AIID-1610.title: Queensland Man Allegedly Distributed Purportedly AI-Generated Sexual Posters Falsely Advertising Women for Sex
AIID-1610.summary: A 52-year-old man in Queensland, Australia, was charged with 43 offences after allegedly using AI to create and distribute posters featuring the faces of at least eight women superimposed onto explicit sexual images. The posters included the victims' personal details, such as names, employment, and social media accounts, and were displayed in public spaces to harass and humiliate them. The campaign, which police described as 'callous and sickening,' spanned from 2021 to 2026.
AIID-1610.description: Queensland police allege that a man used AI to place at least eight women's faces onto explicit images and displayed posters containing their names, social media accounts, employment details, and false claims that they offered sexual services. The alleged campaign ran from February 2021 through May 2026.
